solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Child in old-style school, a learner denied soup

indicators.note: the child abbreviation sits inside what is left of the school word
the school is refused the a and learner letters, so they come out of it

parts.note: a borstal was the old British institution for young offenders, now abolished
L is the learner plate sign on British cars

explanation.surface: A child at a strict old reform school is made to go without soup as a punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: A borstal was a British detention centre for young offenders, abolished in 1982; 'denied' removes A and L to leave BORST.
explanation.definitionFit: Borscht is the beetroot soup of Russia and Ukraine, so the dish is an example of a soup.

clue.text: Retreat of female having returned earlier

indicators.note: the returned word comes before the rest

parts.note: to be back is to have returned

explanation.surface: A woman's withdrawal after she came home early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earlier' places BACK ahead of OF and F.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to withdraw or step down, synonymous with retreating.

clue.text: Wetter prince who married actress

definitions.meaning: Prince ... III of Monaco married Grace Kelly, the film star

explanation.surface: A soppy royal who wed a star of the screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of rainy, and the name of the Monaco prince whose bride was Grace Kelly.

clue.text: Study closely packed bit of reading initially with lens

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
dense means tightly packed together

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the reading word is taken

explanation.surface: A student pores over a densely printed passage with a magnifier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of' joins; 'initially' takes R from reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A condenser is a lens or lens system that concentrates light, as in a microscope or projector.

clue.text: It's not bottled beer, they say, for a man of the Bible

indicators.note: they say signals a word spoken that sounds like another

parts.note: beer that is canned rather than bottled is tinned ale

explanation.surface: A drinker's complaint that his ale came in a can, not a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: TINNED ALE, said out loud, matches the reformer's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: William Tyndale translated the Bible into English in the 1520s, so he is a Bible man.

clue.text: Hounds after the chase perhaps getting food

definitions.meaning: dogs that have been running hard would be heated, panting animals
frankfurters in rolls, sold as a snack

explanation.surface: Hunting dogs, back from the chase, are given something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes the phrase literally: hounds overheated from running. The 'perhaps' flags that playful sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sausages served in a bun are a familiar fast food, sold from street stands.

clue.text: The care about to be given to piece of land?

indicators.note: about means turned around or rearranged, so the letters of the care are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone is about to be put in charge of looking after a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks attached to 'to be given' but is the anagram signal on THE CARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hectare is a metric unit of area, 10,000 square metres, so it measures out a plot of ground.

clue.text: Part of body thus buried under pile of rocks

indicators.note: in a down clue the thus word sits beneath the rocks word

parts.note: a tor is a rocky outcrop on a hilltop, as on Dartmoor
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A body part was found entombed beneath a rockfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buried under' puts SO below TOR in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body, without head and limbs.

clue.text: Group of stars keeping a time for talk

indicators.note: the constellation word holds the a and time letters inside it

parts.note: Orion is the hunter constellation

explanation.surface: A lecture on a constellation, its timing included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' sets A and T inside ORION.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal speech, so it is a talk given to an audience.

clue.text: Remarkable litres emerging from hamper

indicators.note: the litres letter comes out of the hamper word

parts.note: to strangle a thing is to stifle or hamper it
L is the symbol for litre or litres

explanation.surface: Liquid improbably seeping out of a picnic basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hamper' is the verb meaning to stifle, not a basket; 'emerging from' takes L out of STRANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange means odd or out of the ordinary, as something remarkable is.

clue.text: Hair to go round front of nose into area even further down

indicators.note: the go-round-nose piece is put inside the chin word

parts.note: the chin is the part of the face lower still than the nose

indicators.note: the word go wraps around the nose's first letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An instruction to a barber, perhaps, about how hair should sweep around the nose and down towards the chin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'area even further down' is fair because the clue has just mentioned the nose: the face below it is the chin. The two containers nest, making GNO first.
explanation.definitionFit: A chignon is a knot or coil of hair worn at the back of the head, a hairstyle.

clue.text: Historical ship from South Africa protected by fibrous material

indicators.note: the country's letters are sheltered inside the fibre word

parts.note: coir is coconut-husk fibre used for matting and rope
RSA is the Republic of South Africa's abbreviation

explanation.surface: An old ship from South Africa had its cargo packed in protective fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: South Africa is RSA (Republic of South Africa) here, not the more common SA.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair was a Barbary pirate vessel of past centuries, so it is a ship of history.

clue.text: Old French resort not being used for the time being

definitions.text: not being used for the time being

parts.note: Nice is the Riviera resort town

explanation.surface: An old Riviera resort has been mothballed for now.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put in cold storage, held in reserve or postponed, is idiomatically kept in this state.

clue.text: Ancient language a national spouted

indicators.note: spouted words are gushed out in a jumble, so the letters of a national are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone from a country spoke out in an old tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a group of extinct Indo-European tongues of Asia Minor, such as Hittite and Luwian.

clue.text: Imagine possible enemy blockading Red Sea endlessly

indicators.note: the enemy word surrounds the sea letters as a naval blockade would

parts.note: a foe is an adversary, a potential enemy

indicators.note: each of the two words loses its final letter

parts.note: the sea between Africa and Arabia, given as written
the end letter of red
the end letter of sea

explanation.surface: A naval picture: a hostile power might close off the Red Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts both words, leaving RESE, and 'blockading' is the container signal, the enemy surrounding the sea as a fleet would.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee something is to picture it in the mind before it happens, a sense of imagining.

clue.text: Inner quality of ascetic about to be locked up

indicators.note: the about letter is imprisoned inside the sect member's name

parts.note: the Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect of Roman times
C, from circa, is the abbreviation for about

explanation.surface: A hermit's true nature is about to be put behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the abbreviation C, not a preposition; 'to be locked up' puts C inside ESSENE, an ascetic of the ancient Jewish sect.
explanation.definitionFit: Essence is the intrinsic nature of a thing, synonymous with its inner quality.

clue.text: Chemical alert — pet's ill

indicators.note: ill means in a bad way, so the letters are put into a disordered state

parts.note: pet's stands for pet is, its S counted as a letter

explanation.surface: A warning that someone's animal has been taken ill, perhaps by a chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill' rearranges ALERT PETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre is potassium nitrate, a compound used in gunpowder and curing meat.

clue.text: Formality rigid (as you might say!) diminished gradually

indicators.note: the two words of the phrase are swapped round, as one might jokingly say it the other way about

parts.note: red tape is rigid bureaucratic formality

explanation.surface: Some stiff ceremony was gradually toned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as you might say' signals that the two words RED TAPE change places, giving TAPE then RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that tapers narrows or lessens bit by bit, so it has diminished gradually.

clue.text: Up the pole?

parts.note: Up the pole is slang for crazy, but here it means carved high on a tribal post

explanation.surface: Slang for being crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests madness; the answer is literal, describing the carved figures that climb a ceremonial pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Carved emblems stacked up a ceremonial pole are of that kind, relating to the emblems of clans.

clue.text: In the auditorium put down a floor covering

indicators.note: an auditorium is where things are heard, so the words are as spoken

parts.note: to park a thing is to put it down, so put down a is park a

explanation.surface: Someone in a theatre laying down a carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: PARK A spoken ends like the French-style pronunciation, par-kay.
explanation.definitionFit: Parquet is flooring of wooden blocks laid in a pattern, so it covers a floor.

clue.text: Top marksman killed investigator?

parts.note: killed means dead
a private eye is a detective

explanation.surface: A sharpshooter shot a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadeye is an expert shot, someone with deadly accuracy.

clue.text: Fighting body? It'll take one a short distance to get to the front

indicators.note: the shortened distance goes before the other letters
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a mile is a unit of distance
it'll is it will: the it gives its letters and the will take joins
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cryptic sort of riddle about something that carries one person a little way forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims MILE to MIL, and 'to get to the front' puts it ahead of IT, I and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A militia is a citizen army, a body of people trained to fight.

clue.text: Shifting item of furniture? There's hesitation to climb at first

indicators.note: the hesitation comes before the furniture word
in a down clue climbing means read upwards, so the hesitation word goes backwards

parts.note: um is a hesitant sound
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Someone dithers before climbing on a piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to climb' turns UM into MU, and 'at first' places it ahead of TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutable means changeable, liable to shift.

clue.text: Meat in a mouse is more than enough for this bird

indicators.note: the phrase holds more letters than needed, so the bird lies within it

explanation.surface: A mouse is a bigger meal than a small bird needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is more than enough for' says the bird is contained within the longer phrase meaT IN A MOUse.
explanation.definitionFit: The tinamou is a ground-dwelling South American bird, rather like a partridge.

clue.text: Want a change of scene having crossed Belgium

indicators.note: the country letter goes through the middle of the other letters
a change of the word scene means its letters are rearranged

parts.note: B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

explanation.surface: Wanting a new setting, someone travelled over to Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' is the noun meaning lack, not the verb. 'change of' rearranges the scene letters to SENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Absence can mean lack or deficiency, the noun sense of want.

clue.text: Name a good worker who makes life hell for men?

definitions.text: who makes life hell for men?

parts.note: to term is to name or call
an ant is the standard crossword worker insect

explanation.surface: A call to identify a diligent employee, which twists into a bad-tempered character.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a scolding, overbearing woman, a shrew who torments those around her.

clue.text: Excited atmosphere around street

indicators.note: the atmosphere word goes around the street letters

parts.note: air is the atmosphere

explanation.surface: A buzz of excitement fills the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means in a state of commotion or stirred up, roused.

clue.text: Languishes with minimal energy in legs

indicators.note: the energy letter goes inside the legs word

parts.note: pins is slang for legs
E is the physics symbol for energy, a single letter

explanation.surface: Someone wilts, barely able to stand on tired legs.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine is to waste away from longing, the same as languishing.

clue.text: Policeman set free after a while

indicators.note: the freeing word follows the while word

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short while
to untie is to release from bonds

explanation.surface: Someone is released after being held for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a while' is MO, short for moment, as in 'wait a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mountie is a member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police.

clue.text: Son enthralled by cartoon character who plays on a field?

indicators.note: the son is held captive inside the superhero's name

parts.note: Batman is the comic-strip superhero

explanation.surface: A boy is captivated by his favourite cartoon hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enthralled by' sets S inside BATMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman takes strike in cricket, a game played out on a field.

clue.text: Camp using portable bed by lake

parts.note: a cot is a light camp bed
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A campsite set up with folding beds beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A camp in the sense of a faction or clique is a close group, synonymous with a select circle.

clue.text: River engaging engineer

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
cute means charming or engaging

explanation.surface: A river with an engineer at work on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaging' looks like a container word but is the adjective, a synonym of charming.
explanation.definitionFit: To engineer a plan is to carry it out or bring it about, a verb sense of executing it.
